name: up
receiver: Claude running /pith:up, called by the user, by writ or by rn, apart from the caller's conversation.
aim: The caller learns where the work's receiver falls short of a written aim, from what happened when a first user used it once, each point with its place and quoted evidence, in a short result holding only the view and each More, with every Good kept in a result file in form.

name: first-user
receiver: pith's first user agent, given only a work, its receiver and purpose, and essentials files.
aim: It uses the work as its receiver would and reports, for every question, what it did and what happened, without judging and without reading the maker's account.

name: generator
receiver: pith's generator agent, started by writ's or pith's conductor with a plan or the kind of work to write.
aim: It writes the work as agreed, from what it was handed, without guessing a fact or a decision.

name: where
receiver: Claude in writ's or rn's conductor needing pith's files.
aim: The caller learns where pith's essentials, style rules, lint and result form check are.

name: essentials-doc
receiver: pith's first user reading a document as its reader, and writ's generator aiming at it.
aim: Checking a real document with these shows whether its reader can decide and act from it.

name: essentials-readme
receiver: pith's first user reading a README as a newcomer.
aim: Checking a real README with these shows whether a newcomer learns the gain, decides, and starts.

name: essentials-design
receiver: pith's first user using a design document as a maintainer.
aim: Checking a real design document with these shows whether a maintainer can weigh a change by what it costs the user.

name: essentials-prompt
receiver: pith's first user running a prompt with claude -p.
aim: Checking a real prompt with these shows whether the AI acts toward the purpose where no step reaches, and which instructions are not needed.

name: essentials-plugin
receiver: pith's first user running a plugin's README story with claude -p.
aim: Checking a real plugin with these shows whether its user gets what the README promises for what it costs them.

name: essentials-essentials
receiver: pith's first user trying an essentials file on a real work.
aim: Checking a real essentials file with these shows whether it can tell that a work achieved its purpose.
